issue: The standalone 15-min monitor's flap-guard is not a real health check. `lastGoodDeployReachable()` only fetches the Netlify deploys list and returns the id of the second most-recent 'ready' deploy — it never calls assertMoneyPath (or fetches the deploy's content) to confirm that candidate rollback target actually has the correct Stripe link. The result is fed to RollbackController as `lastGoodPasses: Boolean(prev.id)` (line 54), i.e. 'a previous deploy exists' is conflated with 'the previous deploy is healthy'. RollbackController's own docstring invariant (money-path.js:6-7: 'flap guard: never roll back into a last-good that itself fails') is therefore NOT upheld by this caller: if the last two Netlify deploys both contain the wrong Stripe link (e.g. two consecutive bad merges), the monitor will still report lastGoodPasses=true, fire a real Netlify restore into the second bad deploy, and NOT escalate — exactly the flapping scenario the class was built to prevent. Contrast with .github/workflows/netlify-deploy.yml:90-98, which correctly re-runs money-path-smoke.mjs against the restored deploy before declaring success — the immediate deploy-gate has a REAL flap guard, but the continuous monitor (the artifact this PR's execution-notes.md cites as satisfying FIND-003's 'standalone 15-min monitor' requirement) does not.
evidence: apps/landing/scripts/money-path-monitor.mjs:35-42 (lastGoodDeployReachable — no fetch of the candidate deploy's own content, no assertMoneyPath call) and :53 `const d = rc.onResult(verdict.ok, { lastGoodPasses: Boolean(prev.id) })`. apps/life-call/lib/money-path.js:6-7 states the flap-guard invariant this violates. apps/life-call/lib/money-path.test.js:46-52 unit-tests RollbackController's flap-guard branch in ISOLATION (with an explicit `lastGoodPasses:false` param) — it does not, and cannot, catch that the caller mis-derives that param from deploy existence rather than deploy health; no test file exists for money-path-monitor.mjs itself (Glob apps/landing/scripts/*.test.* → no files found).
fix: In lastGoodDeployReachable (or a renamed lastGoodDeployHealthy), fetch the candidate deploy's live content (Netlify deploy-preview URL or the deploy's own domain) and run assertMoneyPath against it — mirroring exactly what netlify-deploy.yml's post-restore reverification does — before passing the result as lastGoodPasses. Add a test file for money-path-monitor.mjs (or extract the health-check as a pure, injectable function) covering the two-consecutive-bad-deploys flap scenario.
